rubric.why: The definition must identify the events or period that make up a cell cycle.
rubric.description: Defines the cell cycle as the series of events from one cell division to the next.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the sequence of events between successive cell divisions, or an equivalent definition involving the cell's growth and division.

rubric.why: Interphase is the period between cell divisions, during which the cell grows and replicates its DNA.
rubric.description: Defines interphase and identifies its main activities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining the period between divisions and/or mentioning growth and DNA replication.

modelAnswer: The cell cycle is the series of events from one cell division to the next.
Interphase is the period between two successive cell divisions, during which the cell grows and replicates its DNA.

items.followUp: What changes occur in prophase-I of meiosis?

rubric.why: The key metaphase-I event is the alignment of homologous chromosome pairs at the cell equator.
rubric.description: States that homologous chromosome pairs (bivalents) line up at the equator.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the arrangement of the pairs at the equator.

rubric.why: Spindle attachment to the chromosomes is another important feature of metaphase-I.
rubric.description: States that spindle fibres attach to the centromeres of the homologous chromosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing spindle-fibre attachment to the centromeres.

modelAnswer: Homologous chromosome pairs (bivalents) arrange themselves at the equator of the cell.
Spindle fibres attach to the centromeres of the chromosomes.

items.followUp: Name two vitamins that are important in human nutrition and state one function of each.

rubric.why: The question asks for two vitamins that act as co-enzymes; examples from the B group and vitamin C are accepted.
rubric.description: Names two suitable vitamins that act as co-enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each correct vitamin name.

modelAnswer: Vitamin B-complex and vitamin C act as co-enzymes.

items.followUp: State two functions of magnesium in plants.

rubric.why: Potassium activates several enzymes in plant cells.
rubric.description: States that potassium activates enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying enzyme activation as a role of potassium.

rubric.why: Potassium also supports important processes such as stomatal movement, protein synthesis, and photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Gives another valid role of potassium in plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one further correct role, such as regulating stomatal opening and closing, protein synthesis, or photosynthesis.

modelAnswer: Potassium activates enzymes in plant cells.
It helps regulate the opening and closing of stomata and is needed for processes such as protein synthesis.

items.followUp: State the functions of red blood cells and plasma.

rubric.why: White blood cells protect the body against disease-causing organisms.
rubric.description: States the defensive function of white blood cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that white blood cells defend the body or fight infection/disease.

rubric.why: Platelets help stop bleeding by forming blood clots.
rubric.description: States the role of platelets in blood clotting.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying clot formation or prevention of blood loss.

modelAnswer: White blood cells defend the body against infection and disease.
Platelets help in blood clotting and prevent excessive blood loss.

items.followUp: Explain how Biology is linked with Medicine, Agriculture, and Computer Science.

rubric.why: Biophysics applies principles and methods of Physics to biological structures and processes.
rubric.description: Explains the link between Biology and Physics.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating physical principles, measurements, or instruments to the study of living things.

rubric.why: Biochemistry studies the chemical substances and reactions occurring in living organisms.
rubric.description: Explains the link between Biology and Chemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating chemical processes or substances to living organisms.

rubric.why: Mathematics and statistics are used to measure, analyse, and interpret biological data.
rubric.description: Explains the link between Biology and Mathematics.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the use of mathematical or statistical methods in Biology.

rubric.why: Biogeography studies where organisms occur and how their distribution relates to geographical conditions.
rubric.description: Explains the link between Biology and Geography.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating the geographical distribution of organisms to Geography.

modelAnswer: Biology is linked with Physics through biophysics, which applies physical principles to living organisms and their processes.
Biology is linked with Chemistry through biochemistry, which studies chemical substances and reactions in living organisms.
Biology is linked with Mathematics through biometry, which uses mathematical and statistical methods to analyse biological data.
Biology is linked with Geography through biogeography, which studies the geographical distribution of plants and animals.

items.followUp: Describe the structure and functions of mitochondria.

rubric.why: The nucleus is enclosed by a double-membraned nuclear envelope.
rubric.description: Describes the nuclear envelope as a double membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the double nuclear membrane.

rubric.why: The envelope has pores, and the nucleus contains nucleoplasm.
rubric.description: Identifies pores in the envelope or the nucleoplasm inside the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct additional structural feature.

rubric.why: The nucleolus and chromatin are important nuclear components; chromatin contains DNA.
rubric.description: Identifies the nucleolus or chromatin/chromosomes containing DNA.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a correct nuclear component and, for chromatin, associating it with DNA.

rubric.why: The nucleus controls and coordinates the activities of the cell.
rubric.description: States that the nucleus controls cell activities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the control function.

rubric.why: The nucleus stores hereditary information; the nucleolus also contributes to ribosome formation.
rubric.description: States a further function of the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying storage/transmission of genetic information or the nucleolus's role in ribosome formation.

modelAnswer: The nucleus is surrounded by a double-membraned nuclear envelope containing pores.
The inside of the nucleus contains nucleoplasm.
Chromatin, made of DNA and proteins, is present in the nucleus and forms chromosomes during cell division.
The nucleus controls and coordinates the activities of the cell.
It stores hereditary information and passes it on to daughter cells; the nucleolus helps form ribosomes.

items.followUp: Describe how ATP is formed during cellular respiration and how its energy is used.

rubric.why: ATP is a nucleotide consisting of adenosine and three phosphate groups; adenosine is adenine joined to ribose.
rubric.description: Describes the molecular composition of ATP.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying adenine, ribose, and three phosphate groups, or an equivalent description.

rubric.why: ATP stores and transfers usable energy in cells and is commonly called the cell's energy currency.
rubric.description: States ATP's role as the cell's energy carrier or energy currency.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing ATP as storing, carrying, or supplying cellular energy.

rubric.why: Energy is associated with the bonds between ATP's phosphate groups, especially the terminal phosphate bond.
rubric.description: Identifies the energy-rich phosphate bonds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for locating stored energy in ATP's phosphate bonds.

rubric.why: Hydrolysis of ATP to ADP and phosphate releases energy for cellular work.
rubric.description: Describes ATP breakdown and energy release.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ATP loses a phosphate to form ADP and releases energy.

rubric.why: ADP can be combined with phosphate to regenerate ATP, using energy supplied by cellular respiration.
rubric.description: Explains that ATP can be regenerated from ADP and phosphate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing ATP regeneration, preferably linking it to energy from respiration.

modelAnswer: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is a nucleotide made of adenine, ribose, and three phosphate groups.
It is the main energy-carrying molecule of the cell and is often called the cell's energy currency.
Energy is stored in the high-energy bonds between its phosphate groups, especially the terminal phosphate bond.
When ATP is hydrolysed, it loses a phosphate group and forms ADP; energy is released for cellular activities.
ADP combines with phosphate using energy from cellular respiration to regenerate ATP.
